subject: Operational proof for non-learning assurance & output entitlements
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rosales <elena.rosales@careix.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational proof for non-learning assurance & output entitlements

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. As discussed, Careix is asking for operational evidence that customer data will not be used to improve models (i.e., no model-training on Careix content), and clarity on output entitlements (who owns responses/derivatives). I wanted to summarize what we can provide immediately and ask what specific artifacts your team needs to close the security review.

What Redwood can provide today (attached):
- redwood_operational_manifest_v1.pdf — a short runbook describing our runtime-level safeguards (prefix exclusion, KV cache eviction, prompt-only ephemeral storage for hosted endpoints).
- redlined_dpa_careix.docx — our proposed DPA language with explicit non-learning commitment and a tailored output-entitlements clause.
- attestation_security_letter.pdf — one-page security attestation describing control checks we can run on request.

Questions for you (to scope the evidence pack):
1) Do you need a signed SOC 2 addendum or is the attestation letter sufficient for legal?
2) Which control IDs or evidence types does Careix want (e.g. system logs showing prefix filtering, retention TTLs, subprocessor inventory with versioned timestamps)?
3) Do you require proof of EU processing locality (runbook + network egress map) vs. a contractual onshore routing guarantee?

We can assemble a short exportable evidence bundle (CSV manifest + redacted log samples + subprocessor list) within 48–72 hours once we have the exact list. If Legal wants specific language around "output entitlements," our legal team can propose two variants (ownership retained by Careix vs. irrevocable license for operational use).

Next steps: happy to hop on a 30-minute bridge with your privacy lead to walk through the manifest and the redline. If that works, suggest Wed 6/16 10:00–10:30 PT.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_operational_manifest_v1.pdf (summary), redlined_dpa_careix.docx (proposed language), attestation_security_letter.pdf (security note)

From: Elena Rosales <elena.rosales@careix.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Careix Legal <legal@careix.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Operational proof for non-learning assurance & output entitlements

On Mon, Jun 14, 2026 at 9:12 AM Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Elena,
> 
> Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. As discussed, Careix is asking for operational evidence that customer data will not be used to improve models...

Hi Jordan — thanks for the quick summary and the attachments. A few asks from our side to make the security and legal review actionable: 

1) Evidence: we need a short, scannable pack with the following concrete items:
   - Subprocessor inventory (name, function, region, first onboarded date).
   - Example log snippet that demonstrates prefix filtering or a non-training tag (redacted).
   - TTL and deletion evidence for ephemeral caches (KV/prefix) and prompt logs.
2) Certification / Attestation: Careix legal typically requires either a SOC 2 addendum or a notarized attestation. Is the attestation_security_letter signed by your Head of Security? If not, can Security provide a signed PDF within the week?
3) Output entitlements: we need the DPA redline to explicitly state that Careix retains exclusive ownership of prompts and responses and that Redwood may only use aggregated telemetry that cannot be associated with Careix customers. A simple clause is fine; Legal will redline if needed.
4) Geo-residency: for EU-subject PHI we require either a contractual guarantee for EU-only processing or a documented operational path (e.g., dedicated EU tenants).

If you can assemble the pack and send over by EOD Wed (6/16) that would keep us on track for our procurement window. Can we confirm the bridge for Wed 6/16 10:00 PT?

Regards,
Elena Rosales
Director, Data Privacy, Careix Health
elena.rosales@careix.com

--
Careix Legal <legal@careix.com> (cc'd)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Operational proof for non-learning assurance & output entitlements — internal action items

Jordan / David — forwarding Elena's asks. Quick task list so we have alignment before the Wed bridge: 

- Jordan: please confirm the bridge time with Elena (10:00 PT Wed) and add Legal (Marissa) if needed.
- David: security to produce a signed attestation (Head of Security signature) and one redacted log snippet showing prefix filtering + TTL policy. Aim for a signed PDF by EOD Tue.
- Kimberly: I'll prepare the subprocessor inventory export (columns: vendor_name, purpose, region, onboarding_date) and a one-page EU processing map.

Notes: for the DPA language on ownership, Legal prefers we offer an exclusive ownership option for customers but also include an operational license for Redwood strictly for servicing and transient caching. If Careix insists on zero-use (no telemetry in aggregate), Legal will escalate to consider an exceptions flow for enterprise.

Keep replies inline so we have a clear audit trail.

Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Security Operations, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rosales <elena.rosales@careix.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Careix Legal <legal@careix.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational proof for non-learning assurance & output entitlements — evidence pack attached

Elena — thanks for the precise list. Attached is the evidence bundle we discussed: 

Attachments included (zipped as evidence_bundle_careix_20260616.zip):
- redwood_operational_manifest_v1.pdf — runbook describing how the non-learning flag is applied at request-time and how ephemeral prompt/response storage is scoped.
- subprocessor_inventory_careix.csv — export with vendor name, function, region, and onboard date (redwood internal ids removed).
- prefix_filter_log_example.txt (redacted) — small log snippet showing a non-training-tagged request; timestamps truncated and PII removed.
- attestation_security_letter.pdf — signed by Head of Security, Ana Mercer (signed PDF).
- redlined_dpa_careix.docx — our proposed contractual changes with the "non-learning" commitment and an output-entitlements clause that makes ownership explicit.

Links:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cCAREIX_PROOF
- Docusign (DPA redline): https://www.docusign.com/partner/embedded?envelopeId=abc123-def456

We can walk through the manifest on the Wed 10:00 PT call. If Legal wants a single-sentence "no-derivatives" phrase replaced with "exclusive output entitlements," we can propose language live and follow with a short addendum to the DPA.

If anything in the bundle is insufficient, call out exactly which control or sample you need and we'll iterate.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments sent: evidence_bundle_careix_20260616.zip (contains the three PDFs, CSV, and log example).
